changed.what: The seed done-condition's second part (an attribution of the session cited as established is refused with FROB-REF-880) was an acceptance criterion with no unit test, so the bead could close with the citation path untested. Added `session_citation_refused_880`: N27b-15's guard in the role Established gives 880, exit 3, with its fields and three ranked repairs, and the role Described is admitted with the permitted wording.

The planted failures ran under `--negative-controls`, an option that exists nowhere (STD-E2E), and needed build flags that no product binary can carry (N38b-04), so the script could not be written. They are now the gates' registered mutation controls (the fork stepping past its checkpoint, N27a-06; design changes mapped to exogenous, N27a-07). The script's last step runs them with `e2e_tier g5_determinism GATE-AUTOPSY-01 --mutations` and `e2e_tier g1_known_answers GATE-AUTOPSY-02 --mutations`, asserts `caught` from the receipts, records nothing, and has an acceptance line. The fallback `frob eval run …` is now the full single-task form (task, --worlds, --run-seed, --tier, --key, no --battery), so the implementer cannot drop the task or add --battery, which gives 802.

The FROB-REF-584 envelope's `required` lacked the class clause that N27-REF's row has ("at class D2 or better"), and the repairs lacked the row's class-clause repair (re-run under a profile with a current class-D2 record). The handler would have emitted fields that differ from the registry, and N27b-16's row check would fail. The repair's `frob run fork` command now carries `--key <k> --json` (convention 5).

The record step omitted N38a-09 rule 2a (the result's receipt committed at receipts/pilots/<hash>.json in the same commit), so the loader would refuse the appended result with `pilot-receipt-uncommitted`. Added to the record step and to acceptance. Corrected the claim that the fallback 'is of a lower tier, as the register requires': for a tier-S record, rule 5 requires a Solid fallback. The C11-script note is a false alarm: the test plan already says that the pilot script runs outside the product.

Applied H-verbs-6's ANSWER. Step 5 now names the commands: `frob report run <run> --cite <claim> --json` (Established) and `--claim reality --cite <claim>` (Reality), both 880 with exit 3, and the uncited report prints the described wording. Acceptance matches. The ANSWER's `--key` was not applied: report.run is a `read` verb (VERBS-report), where `--key` is FROB-REF-802 (NJL-01). The `--negative-controls` option does not exist; it is now E2E_PLANT_FAILURE plants declared as `plants=dry-patch,altered-verdict`. The 'build flag that lets gear_ratio through' cannot be planted in a product binary; it is GATE-AUTOPSY-02's registered control 'design changes mapped to exogenous' (N27a-07). BD-302 was not added as a dependency: N27b-18 already depends on it transitively (via BD-284 → … → N37-26 → BD-302).

The bead said that 'the end-to-end helper gains a step `autopsy_audit`', but the shared lib.sh is reserved for `e2e_` functions (STD-E2E), and a shell step had no way to call the Rust auditor. The hook is now the bead's own library `scripts/e2e/lib/autopsy.sh`, named in scope, whose `autopsy_audit <dir>` calls the example target `cargo run -p frob-autopsy --example autopsy_audit -- <dir> --json` (DESIGN) and logs through the shared functions. The test plan says the auditor is reached by no frob command.

The C11-script note holds in part: the test plan said 'No script of its own' without the reason convention 11 requires. It now says that the bead delivers nothing a frob command can reach (tier entries, binding table, fixture tests, derivations). The rest was checked and is right: every bound test name exists in its bead, the thermal and growth arithmetic recomputes (37.95 s, 113.28 °C, 42.42 s, 81.98 °C; 24.5, 601.6, 3.62e5), and the deps are sound.

Record step and acceptance lacked N38a-09 rule 2a (receipt committed at receipts/pilots/<hash>.json), so the result would be refused `pilot-receipt-uncommitted`; added. The C11-script note was right that the test plan gave no reason for the absence of a scripts/e2e script; it now states the pilot has no product dependency and delivers nothing a frob command can reach. All figures recomputed and correct (G ≤ 1,666.7; 46.4 steps, 1.16 s; 247 steps; ceilings 4.0, 2.98, 3.24; λ 0.16 per step = 6.4 s⁻¹).

The gate measurement relied on 'k = 1', but k (one in eight) has no verb input or policy setting, so the script could not set it. The e2e line now says the gate script runs every admitted case's double-precision repeat itself (`--lane f64`) and compares by this bead's rule of step 3; matches N27b-28. Clopper–Pearson bounds (0.851, 0.928, 0.898), the alarm counts and the 800-identity selection band recomputed and correct.

Stage 4 runs the numerical-variant interventions of N27b-25 first for admitted failures that double precision does not reproduce, but N27b-25 was not a dependency, so the bulk planner could be built before the mechanism it calls. Added dep N27b-25 (M3, no cycle: graph_check reports none). Cost model, worked instance (704,000 world-seconds; 176/704/7,040 s) and ceilings (4.0, 2.98, 3.24) recomputed and correct.

(1) GATE-AUTOPSY-03 had two recorders, this bead and N27b-09 (convention 9; N38b-15 names N27b-09). This bead now records only GATE-AUTOPSY-09 and writes the lane clause into its receipt for N27b-09's entry to read. Scope, background and acceptance are aligned. (2) The 'k = 1' cross-check cannot be set; the script runs the double-precision repeats itself with `--lane f64` and compares by N27b-26's rule. (3) The table's commands lacked the fork or run handle, `--world`, and `--key` on run verbs; they are spelled in full now (read verbs without --key). (4) `--negative-controls` does not exist: the plants are now `plants=self-crosscheck,no-ceiling` under E2E_PLANT_FAILURE. The 'admission bypassed by a build flag' control is the gate's registered mutation control, planted by the tier run (`e2e_tier … --mutations`) and asserted `caught` from E2E_LAST_RECEIPT.

requests.what: Test plan line 141: the script's planted failures run 'with `--negative-controls`', an option that exists nowhere (STD-E2E: plants are declared in the header `plants=` and injected under E2E_PLANT_FAILURE), and its build-flag defects cannot be planted in a product binary (N38b-04). Turn the script-level plants into E2E_PLANT_FAILURE plants and assert the build-level ones as the gate's registered mutation controls, `caught` in the tier run's receipt. Otherwise the script calls a nonexistent option and `--verify-plants` cannot exercise it. Also note that N27b-28 now leaves the GATE-AUTOPSY-03 row to N27b-09 alone and writes the lane clause into its GATE-AUTOPSY-09 receipt for N27b-09's entry to read.

Test plan line 120: 'Planted defects the script must catch (`--negative-controls`): a build flag …' has the same two defects as N27b-09: a nonexistent option and build flags that no product binary carries (N38b-04). Use E2E_PLANT_FAILURE plants for what the script can plant, and the owning gates' registered mutation controls, asserted from receipts, for build-level defects.
